occurrences.operation: Racial-colonial embodied history makes mask meaningful; no generic disguise allegory can replace its source world.

returns.operation: Language and racialising gaze impose a mask whose lived refusal cannot be replaced by a generic avatar.
Recognition preserves the other’s irreducibility under an imposed image.

rows.figures: Colonial language/status; Antillean speaker; metropolitan French; white gaze; lived Black body; historico-racial schema; epidermal racial schema; imposed mask; recognition field
